title: Evidence-based evaluation rubric
summary: Use this template to evaluate an AI system against explicit criteria, retain evidence for every judgment, and identify results that cannot yet support a decision. It also provides remediation paths for missing, ambiguous, or conflicting evidence.
prerequisites: A defined use case and the decision the evaluation must inform
Representative evaluation cases with expected outcomes
Access to the outputs and records that will serve as evidence

sections.title: Answer and source correction
paragraphs: Practitioner question: How do I make an AI evaluation rubric produce evidence that another reviewer can verify? For this intermediate-level template, define the decision and unacceptable failures first, evaluate representative cases against explicit criteria, attach an observation to every judgment, and treat unsupported judgments as not assessed rather than guessing.

The previous citation, content/resources/evaluation-safety/evidence-based-evaluation-rubric.json, was an unregistered internal path and had never been verified. The citation record has been corrected to the National Institute of Standards and Technology publication listed in Sources. This change affects the source provenance and the wording connecting the template to documented measurement and risk-management practices; the rubric procedure and expected evidence remain unchanged.
sections.callout: A score without a traceable observation is not sufficient evidence. Record what happened, which criterion it addresses, and how it affected the decision.

sections.title: Apply the rubric
paragraphs: Step 1: State the intended use, the decision this evaluation will inform, and the failures that would make the result unacceptable. If reviewers cannot agree on the scope or unacceptable failures, narrow the use case or create separate rubrics, assign a decision owner, and do not begin scoring until that owner approves the scope.

Step 2: Assemble representative cases and record the expected outcome or review standard for each case. If a case has no defensible expected outcome, flag the evidence gap, obtain an adjudicated expectation from the responsible reviewer, and exclude that case from any overall conclusion until it is resolved.

Step 3: Evaluate each case against every applicable criterion and retain the observed output or behavior supporting the judgment. If the required evidence is unavailable or ambiguous, record the criterion as not assessed, identify the missing evidence, and rerun the case after that evidence becomes available.

Step 4: Establish the decision rule before interpreting the collected results. If the rule has no documented rationale or responsible owner, pause the decision, document how the rule relates to the intended use and unacceptable failures, and obtain approval from the decision owner before applying it.

Step 5: Review failed and not-assessed criteria before accepting the result, then test any corrective change against the same relevant cases. If the change introduces a regression or leaves required evidence unavailable, reject or revise the change and repeat the affected evaluation.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a completed rubric record that identifies the intended use, decision owner, unacceptable failures, evaluated cases, applicable criteria, observed outputs or behaviors, criterion-level judgments, evidence gaps, remediation actions, decision rule, and overall conclusion.

Verify traceability by selecting each judgment and following it to the recorded observation and applicable criterion. If a judgment lacks either link, change it to not assessed, record what evidence is missing, and obtain or reproduce that evidence before using the judgment.

Verify decision readiness by checking that every failed or not-assessed criterion has a stated effect on the overall conclusion and a responsible next action. If any item has no next action or owner, withhold the overall decision and assign remediation or evidence collection before review resumes.

Verify repeatability by giving the rubric record and retained evidence to another qualified reviewer and asking whether the same decision rule can be applied without unstated assumptions. If the reviewer cannot reproduce the reasoning, clarify the criterion, expected outcome, evidence reference, or decision rule and repeat the review.
